dedupe_keys.name: hedwige and prosper polders transboundary depoldering sigma plan scheldt

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the depoldering of the Hertogin Hedwige polder in the Netherlands and the Prosper polder in Belgium on the Scheldt estuary under the Belgian Sigma Plan. The outer defences of these reclaimed polders are being removed to reopen 465 hectares (295 Dutch, 170 Belgian) to the tides, giving room to storm surges and creating brackish intertidal nature next to the Saeftinghe wetlands. A new inland ring dike about 10.2 m above NAP, a ring canal and a fish-friendly pumping station protect the residential hinterland. Cost-benefit analysis for the Dutch government put the Hedwige option at 40.0 to 49.3 million euros and Prosper at 25.8 million euros, mostly paid by Flanders under the Scheldt Agreements; for the Sigma Plan as a whole, such projects were more cost-effective than a large storm surge barrier. Completion was expected in 2023, and the site also serves as the Interreg Polder2C's living lab for levee and emergency response experiments. The page, published in 2016 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with links to the Sigma Plan. Caveats: sedimentation could be too high for the objectives, and Dutch opposition delayed the work. It illustrates nature-based storm surge and flood hazard reduction and climate adaptation; related records are the Kruibeke Bazel Rupelmonde and Hesketh Out Marsh case studies.
